correctness.rationale: All connected nonempty allocations on a star have one hub bundle with exactly r=k-n+1 chosen leaves and n-1 singleton leaf bundles. For a neighboring singleton j, its exact connected two-way share is max over isolating one leaf i of min(w_i,H+w_j-w_i). A strict improvement exists exactly when selected i and outside j satisfy w_i>w_j and H>w_i. This yields sorted-leaf choices or h=0 and at most one positive selected leaf. Counting tie classes gives Q_r; labels give n!Q_r. Any violating inversion permits a leximin-improving swap. Fair allocations share an identical sorted utility vector, establishing the converse, including r=0, r=k, zero weights and ties. Independently reconstructed 6,012 exact finite (k,weight,hub,r) settings, checking direct pair shares, leximin and Q_r.
